**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 94, verse 1:**

(p-115) **Surat al-Sharh (The Expansion): its purpose**

It details the blessing mentioned at the end of Surat al-Duha, and it explains that what is meant by "reporting" (al-tahdith) it is gratitude for it, through devotion to Allah and turning toward Him by remembering His kindness and His great mercy, by describing Him with lordship (al-Rububiyyah) and acknowledging His favours. Its name, al-Sharh, indicates this, as does "In the name of Allah," whose command is exalted and whose majesty is high, and there is no god but Him, so great is the bounty He has bestowed. "The Most Merciful" (al-Rahman), whose generosity overflows upon all His creation, because He is the Lord of Majesty and Honour. "The Most Compassionate" (al-Rahim), who, by His special mercy, brings the people of His presence to the highest station within the stations of distinction.

* *

When He commanded him (ﷺ) at the end of the morning (al-Duha) to report His blessing, which He had bestowed upon him, He detailed it in this surah. He said, affirming it in the form of a rhetorical question of denial, for emphasis in affirming it to those who deny it, and in establishing it, presenting the favour of the expansion (al-sharh) in its form before announcing the forgiveness, as He did in Surat al-Fath, which is the result of the expansion. So that the good news of honour would come first, drawing the speech toward the manifestation of greatness, magnifying the expansion.

**"Did We not expand (for you)"** i.e., an expansion befitting Our greatness (p-116) **"for you"** i.e., specifically.

When He specified the one for whom the expansion was done, but the expansion itself was vague, the soul's longing for it increased, so that it would be more grand for him. He explained it, so that it would be an explanation after vagueness, making it greater in exalting it and more honoured in making known its matter. So He said: **"your breast"** i.e., We gladden it and delight it with the emigration (al-hijrah). This surah is Meccan according to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and We honour it and magnify it, and We remove from it (your heart) and split it open and wash it and fill it with faith, wisdom, tenderness, knowledge and mercy. So it became very wide, enough to embrace intimate communion with the Truth and the call to the creation. It was with the Truth in its greatness and elevation, and with the creation through the overflow of its lights and rays. This expansion was literal many times, and it was also figurative through the lodging of all its meanings. All of this is beyond description. I will not express to you about it except by a report that it was split by Our greatness. The knowledge through which it was split is the knowledge of Allah, the Hereafter, the religion and the world. The wisdom which flowed in it is placing a thing in its proper place and giving every person with a right his right.

Abu Ja'far al-Mansur recited **"We expand"** with a fatha on the ha' (nashrah), and Ibn 'Atiyyah explained it as emphasis with the light nun, then he changed the alif from the nun, then he deleted the nun for lightness. Abu Hayyan said that al-Lihyani related in his Nawadir from some Arabs the nasb with lam and the jazm with lan. (p-117) Its secret here is that the fatha in pronunciation is extremely appropriate to the expansion. The reading of the majority (al-Jumhur) is that when it indicates the fatha through the expansion, it indicates through the jazm that, together with that, it is a binder of the judgment it deposited and a controller of it, guiding by what is in it of the solidity of knowledge and the dignity of piety and forbearance. Ibn Burjan said: He distinguished between the Prophet and the walí in this, that the Prophet had his breast expanded outwardly, so he rose outwardly, and the walí had that expanded inwardly, so he was elevated inwardly. The disbeliever had that constricted, and it remained with its darkness and the portions of Satan in it, so he cannot accept guidance nor ascend in the paths of contemplation except to the measure of his ability to ascend into the sky. **"Thus Allah places the uncleanness upon those who do not believe"** (al-An'am 6:125), and so on, the verses.

And since breadth of breast through knowledge and wisdom is beauty by the gathering of excellences, and that was accompanied by bearing what is among the greatest of burdens, and beauty through the gathering of excellences is not perfected except when it combines with beauty the majesty (jalal) of the absence of blemishes, and since the interrogative of denial (al-istifham al-inkari), when it is joined with negation, becomes affirmation, because it is a negation of a negation, He said, conjoining to it what is conjoined only with affirmation: ﴿And We removed﴾, that is, We lowered, dropped and nullified, a lowering that has no return and no possibility of return in any way, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿from you your burden﴾, that is, your heavy load which cannot be borne. For this reason (p-118) He described it by His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 94, verse 3:

﴿Who weighed down your back﴾. That is, [He made it so]. The back is the pillar of the body, its joints creaking from the weight, as a new saddle creaks when it is loaded with a heavy burden. This was what overwhelmed him when he was commanded to warn his people and confront them with what they hated: denouncing the defects of their religion, showing their fathers to be misguided, and calling their wisdom foolish for adopting a religion that no intelligent person would accept if he reflected on it even briefly, free of self-interest. They also had their pride, their zealotry, and their readiness to throw themselves into destruction at the slightest anger. So he said:

"My Lord, if so, they will crush my head and leave it like a loaf of bread."

God, glorified and exalted, lightened this for him through the marvels He showed him and the miracles with which He strengthened him, and He guaranteed him protection in matters whose full extent no one knows except the One who strengthened him with them. ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67], until that burden became light for him. His closest family became the most solicitous of him, preventing him from some of his preaching and holding on to his garment so that he would not go out to them and say what he said, which would bring upon him what he disliked. He would then pull himself free from them and go out to them and inform them, as happened in the matter of the Night Journey and other events.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "It means that Jibril, upon him be prayers and peace, split open his chest, took out his heart, cleansed it, removed from it a black clot, washed it, and then filled it with knowledge, faith, and wisdom." That is, he came to bear what others could not bear, and what weighs on others was made light for him. (p-119) There is no doubt that this is a linguistic burden, which is clear, and a legal burden in terms of wealth, on the assumption of abandoning the obligatory compliance because of its heaviness. Allah has protected him from that.

Al-Ustadh (the teacher) Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: The meaning of this surah is connected to the meaning of the surah before it, and the sum of the two surahs is an enumeration of Allah's blessings upon him, glorified and exalted. If you say: why did you separate Surah Alam Nashrah (Surah al-Sharh) and not mention these blessings together in one surah? I say: It is customary among humans, when someone enumerates blessings to his son or servant, to first mention those that the listener witnessed and that were caused by something he did, some of which may be understood as a reward rather than a gift from the outset. Then, when he has fulfilled his purpose in this, he follows it with blessings that were given to him as a beginning, which existed before his own existence. For example, a father says to his son: "Did I not choose for you a mother and provision when I begot you, and prepare for your benefits such and such?" A parallel to what we have pointed to is His saying, glorified, to Zakariyya, upon him be prayers and peace: ﴿And you were nothing﴾ [Maryam: 9]. He first mentioned to him, "We give you good news of Yahya," and the idea that the human acquisition (kasb) alone brings about the existence of a child (the view of the Kasbiyya, those who attribute such effects to human acquisition) was not hidden from one whose vision is limited and who is not guided. So He began by mentioning it, then followed it with what could not possibly be misunderstood in that way, which is His saying: ﴿And I created you before, when you were nothing﴾ [Maryam: 9]. There are parallels to this in the Books, and the verses of these two surahs came in this manner. (p-120) And Allah knows best. End.

When He honored him within himself with a perfection that combined majesty with majesty, and this honor is not pure except together with nobility in the eyes of people, He said: ﴿And We raised﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness and overpowering power, ﴿for you﴾, that is, specifically, an elevation before which the elevation of every other creature is effaced, ﴿your remembrance﴾ among all the worlds, rational and otherwise, through truthfulness, trustworthiness, forbearance, gravity, noble character, purity of disposition, and freedom from every blemish of deficiency. So much so that, before prophethood, your fame among your people was only "the Trustworthy" (al-Amin), and they would cite your pure qualities and your resplendent, brilliant attributes as an example. Then came prophethood, then messengerhood, then the Hijra (emigration). And We made your name joined with Our name in the word of tawhid (kalimat al-tawhid, the declaration of God's oneness), in faith, in the adhan (call to prayer), the iqamah (second call to prayer), the tashahhud (testimony recited in prayer), and the khutbah (sermon), so that I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned along with Me. Among the honors is victory over your enemies and honor for your allies. Your pleasure was made My pleasure, and your obedience was made My obedience. I commanded My angels to send blessings upon you, and I address you with lofty titles and exalted, honoring marks, such as "the Messenger" and "the Prophet" and the like, according to the styles of speech and the fitting of constructions, besides other virtues, merits and qualities that cannot be encompassed by description.

Al-Razi said: Then He gave his community the greatest share of that. "It was said: O Messenger of God, who are the friends of God? He said: 'Those who, when they are remembered, God is remembered.'" [And in another hadith: "Those who, when they are seen, God is remembered."] He also said: "The best of you are those who, when seen, make you remember God, whose speech increases your knowledge, and whose deeds make you indifferent to the world." So the ultimate of the division of praise is that He mixed His remembrance with his remembrance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 94, verse 5:

When he mentioned these noble attainments, which are perfection, and perfection is not made pure except with the assistance of destinies (al-aqdar), for lofty aspirations, when they are great, their fields of action expand, and if there occurs in them some obstruction, there occurs in them the distress of their own nature [it expanded], he explained that He removed from him the obstacles, in an expression indicating that the cause of the bestowal of these perfections was what he (ﷺ) had of patience in the face of troubles and his swallowing of the bitterness of destinies. He said, emphasizing, encouraging the bearing of the like of that, hoping for reward with what befits these lofty ranks, strongly urging its endurance, by mentioning the "with" (al-ma'iyyah), indicating the closeness of the two periods, such that they were as if mutually inseparable, causing what had been mentioned of his condition from the Morning (al-Duha): ﴿Indeed﴾, that is, He, glorified is He, did these great perfections for you because He had decreed in eternity a decree that cannot be turned back, [nor is there any repealer] of any part of it, that ﴿with hardship﴾, that is, [this] type specifically, ﴿is ease﴾, that is, very great ease, through which He brings about benefits and expands what had been constrained of the faculties. For the people of trials have always awaited ease, knowing from the primordial nature (al-fitrah al-ula) upon which people were created that He is the Sole One with perfection, and that He is the Doer by choice, who adorns existents with their opposites. Glorified and exalted is He, He has carried out His ancient custom that relief comes with distress. When he (ﷺ) endured what was mentioned in the Morning of severe orphanhood and the misguidance of his people, the Arabs especially, all of them, whom Allah, exalted is He, inspired him to oppose in the root of the religion by avoiding the idols, and in its branch by standing with the people at 'Arafah during Hajj in the station of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and of poverty such as no one had borne, until he reached a state in which Glorified and Exalted He bestowed favor upon him by rescuing him from it in His ancient Book and His wise Remembrance. And he, while bearing all that, was standing with what was due to him of patience and rising to the lofty heights of gratitude, "he bears the burdens," as the Greatest Truthful One (al-Siddiqah al-Kubra), Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "the destitute, he hosts the guest, he maintains the ties of kinship, and he aids in the calamities of truth."

Then he bore the burdens of prophethood, and he met from his people harm, distress and trials such as no one else had borne. Allah, exalted is He, gave him the good news that He would make all of that easy for him and soften their hearts, so that his religion would prevail over all religion, and would enrich his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, after their poverty, multiply them after their fewness, and grant them honor after their humiliation, and these opponents of his would become the greatest of supporters, and the opponent would submit to him in the most complete submission, and He would open for him the greatest of lands, so that this bestowal in ease would be in proportion to what had befallen him of hardship. For He, glorified and exalted, decreed a decree that will not be reversed, that He alternates between conditions, as a decisive proof that He, exalted is He, alone is the Doer, and that His action is by choice, not by essence and compulsion.

When difficulty was disliked by souls, and God, glory be to Him, had great wisdoms in it, and wisdoms are not manifest except to individual servants, He repeated it, glory be to Him, by way of resumption (*istinaf*, a new sentence that answers an implied question), answering one who says: "Is there any difficulty after it?" Emphasizing it, encouraging attention to His command, anticipating what results from it, and giving good news by its repetition, even though the difficulty is one, and though it is possible that each of the two be understood as something other than what the other intends. So He said: ﴿Indeed, with difficulty﴾, meaning the one mentioned, for it is definite (*ma'rifah*), and a definite term, when repeated as a definite term, is other than the first, whether the reference intended is the previously mentioned (*'ahd*) or the category (*jins*). ﴿Ease﴾, meaning another, to remove harms and hardships. For an indefinite term (*nakirah*), when repeated as an indefinite term, may be other than the first. The Prophet ﷺ said: "It is other than it." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Ease has come to you; difficulty will never overcome two eases." He narrated this through many routes. ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "If difficulty were in the hole of a lizard, ease would follow it until it brought it out." [And al-Tabarani narrated from him, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If difficulty were in a hole, ease would enter upon it until it brought it out."] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the verse. The hafiz Nur al-Din al-Haythami said: In its chain is Abu Malik al-Nakhaʿi, who is weak. Al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Awsat, and al-Bazzar, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, with similar wording. Al-Haythami said: In its chain is ʿAʾidh ibn Shurayh, who is weak. Al-Farra' narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ "went out one day while laughing and saying: 'Difficulty will never overcome two eases.'" ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from Maʿmar, from Ayyub, from al-Hasan, with it, as a mursal (a report lacking a companion in its chain). From his route al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab narrated it. [And] al-Tabari narrated it through the route of Ibn Thawr from Maʿmar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another route, connected (*mawsul*), and its chain is weak. On the subject there is also a report from ʿUmar, which Malik mentioned in al-Muwatta' from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that it reached him that Abu ʿUbaydah, may Allah be pleased with him, was present in Syria, so he wrote to him a letter in which was: "Difficulty will never overcome two eases." Al-Hakim narrated it through his route. Our shaykh Ibn Hajar said this in his takhrij of the hadiths of al-Kashshaf, and said: This is the most authentic of its routes. End. And this is from the standpoint that ease is indefinite and difficulty is definite. It is well known that when an indefinite term is repeated as an indefinite term, the second is other than the first, and the definite is the reverse. The Shaykh Saʿd al-Din al-Taftazani said at the beginning of his *Talwih*, in discussing the definite and the indefinite: (p-125) The discussion concerns when the first expression is repeated either with its mode of indefiniteness or definiteness, or without them. In that case, the means of definiteness is either the article (*al-*) or annexation (*idafah*), so that it is valid to repeat a definite as indefinite and vice versa. The detail of this is that the term mentioned first is either indefinite or definite, and on either assumption it is either repeated as indefinite or as definite, making four categories. The rule is to look at the second: if it is indefinite, it is other than the first; otherwise the appropriate reading is definiteness, on the basis that it is a previously mentioned referent. If it is definite, it is the first, taking it as referring to the known referent, which is the basic meaning of the article and annexation. He mentioned in *al-Kashf* that when an indefinite is repeated as indefinite, the second is other than the first; otherwise it is its very self, because the definite encompasses the whole category, while the indefinite covers a part, so it falls within the whole, whether it is placed first or last. In this there is room for examination. First, because definiteness does not necessarily signify comprehensiveness; rather the referent (*ʿahd*) is the basic meaning, and when a previously mentioned referent exists, the indefinite need not be that same referent. Second, because the meaning of the second being the very first is that the intended object of the second is the intended object of the first, and a part in relation to the whole is not like that. Third, because repeating a definite as an indefinite while the second differs from the first is frequent in speech. God, exalted, said: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete﴾ [al-An'am: 154], up to His saying: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down﴾ [al-An'am: 155]. He, exalted, said: ﴿Descend, some of you being enemies to others﴾ [al-A'raf: 24]. He, exalted, said: ﴿And He raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ [al-An'am: 165], and other than these. Another said: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾, and from this is the poet's saying:

*When people are people, and time is time*

For if the second were the very first, there would be no benefit in reporting it. End.

He said: Know that what is meant is that this is the basic rule when unqualified and when the context lacks indicators. Otherwise an indefinite may be repeated without difference, as in His saying, exalted: ﴿And He is the One who in heaven is God, and on earth is God﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84]. ﴿And they said: Why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord? Say: Indeed Allah is able to send down a sign﴾ [al-An'am: 37]. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength, then He made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ [al-Rum: 54], meaning the strength of youth. From this is the category of verbal emphasis (*tawkid lafzi*). An indefinite may also be repeated as definite with difference, as in His saying: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾ [al-An'am: 155], up to His saying: ﴿lest you say: The Book was sent down only upon two groups before us﴾ [al-An'am: 156]. Another said: ﴿There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves, a settlement, and settlement is good﴾ [al-Nisa': 128], where the indefinite refers to the specific, which is settlement between the spouses, and the definite refers to the general, every lawful settlement. ﴿We shall increase their punishment, a punishment upon punishment﴾ [al-Nahl: 88], for a thing cannot be upon itself. End.

He said: A definite may also be repeated as definite with difference, as in His saying, exalted: [﴿And We have sent down to you the Book with truth, confirming what is before it of the Book﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48]. Another said]: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26]. The first is general and the second specific. ﴿Is the recompense of good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60]. The first is the deed and the second the reward. ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that the soul is for the soul﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45]. The first is the killer and the second the one killed. End. He said: A definite may also be repeated as indefinite without difference, as in His saying, exalted: ﴿That your God is one God﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108], and similar examples are many. A definite is like an indefinite in the two states of repetition: when a definite is repeated as definite, the second is the first, and when repeated as indefinite, it is other. Then he gave the example of the verse here, and said: This is based on the premise that the indefinite ﴿ease﴾ is for magnification, and the definite ﴿difficulty﴾ is for the referent, that is, the difficulty you are in, or the category, that is, what everyone knows. So the second ease is other than the first, unlike difficulty. End. In *al-Kashshaf* he said: As for ease, it is indefinite, covering some part of the category. So when the second statement is a new sentence following an indefinite that covered some part, it covers a part other than the first part, without difficulty.

(p. 128) When he (al-Biqa'i) knew from this that provisions are proportioned to the severity of the tasks, because of the gratitude owed by the one who is provided for, and when he knew the promise of increase for the grateful, he said, as a consequence of the ease bestowed after that hardship, urging him to gratitude and informing him that he does not cease to bear some burden for God: ﴿When you have finished﴾, i.e., when you have finished, by the ease He has given you, with the ease of your struggle in which you are at the time of this address, which entails hardship in the outcome or in the present state. Hardship follows it wherever it is, especially when people enter the religion in multitudes, or from the heavy, great worship of receiving and bearing the revelation, or from the aim of the ease that We have promised you. ﴿then strive hard﴾, i.e., exert yourself to the utmost in toil through another form of worship, such as glorifying God (tasbih) and seeking forgiveness (istighfar), or voluntary prayer (nafl), for the One who has granted you this favour.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 94, verse 8:

﴿And to your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has bestowed favour upon you through what He mentioned in these two surahs in particular, ﴿so turn eagerly﴾, that is, by asking, because He alone is the Capable, just as He alone was capable of nurturing you in the past. He alone is distinguished by greatness, so there is no power at all except in the One who gives a person what he desires from it. Eagerness (al-raghb) is always the emblem of the servant in every state. That is, do this. ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh: 1]. Thus this last part is connected to the first in the connection of the effect (ma'lul) to its cause (ʿillah), and what follows it is likewise harmonized with it in precisely that way (p-129), like the harmony of the sun with the crescent moons. The end of this surah points to striving in worship upon finishing the struggle (jihad) against the disbelievers in the Arabian Peninsula (Jazirat al-Arab), after the passing of a number of years equal to the number of verses of this surah following the Hijra (migration), which are eight, out of desire for the Hereafter, which is [better] than the former, indicating the nearness of the appointed term by what the surah of Victory (al-Nasr) points to, as will come, God willing, Most High.
